title: Tenali and the Dream Merchant

full_text:
A traveling trickster named Mayan arrived in the bustling market of Vijayanagara, setting up an opulent velvet tent adorned with colored glass lanterns. He proclaimed to the curious townspeople:
'I am the Master Dream Merchant! For a single gold coin, I will sell you a fragrant herbal incense that will grant you whatever dream you desire—to be an emperor, to discover mountains of emeralds, or to fly across the stars!'

Many foolish youths and gullible citizens paid gold coins, burned the incense, dreamed extravagant dreams, and woke up to find their purses empty and their daily chores neglected.

Tenali Raman decided to bring an end to this deceptive trade.
He walked into the tent, paid one gold coin, and said:
'Master Mayan, sell me a dream of becoming the sole sovereign of Vijayanagara, seated upon the Golden Throne, commanding all the treasuries and armies.'

Mayan handed Tenali a pinch of scented sandalwood powder: 'Burn this tonight, and thy dream is guaranteed!'

The next morning, Tenali arrived at the tent accompanied by four royal guards with drawn swords!
Tenali pointed at Mayan: 'Arrest this man for high treason!'

Mayan trembled in terror: 'Treason? What have I done, Master Tenali?'
Tenali declared in a booming, authoritative voice:
'Last night, I burned thy incense. In my dream, I became the absolute Emperor of Vijayanagara! As Emperor, I reviewed the royal accounts and discovered that thou hast been operating an illegal lottery within my empire without paying the imperial license fee of five thousand gold dinars!
Pay the five thousand gold dinars to the imperial guards immediately, or be marched to the citadel dungeon!'

Mayan cried out in despair:
'Master Tenali! It was only a dream! How can you arrest a real man for a decree issued in a dream?'

Tenali smiled with razor-sharp irony:
'Why, Master Merchant? If thy dreams are real enough to demand real gold coins from innocent citizens, then the imperial decrees issued inside those dreams are real enough to demand real fines!
Confess that dreams are illusions of no commercial value, return every stolen coin to the people, and leave Vijayanagara forever!'

Terrified, the Dream Merchant unlocked his iron cashbox, returned every single gold coin to the cheated townspeople, packed his tent, and fled the empire.
The citizens cheered Tenali, realizing that those who profit from illusions must be defeated with their own phantoms.
moral: Deceptive peddlers who sell imaginary illusions must be paid with mirror reflections.

quiz.question: What fundamental virtue is highlighted in "Tenali and the Dream Merchant"?
options: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
Acting in hasty anger without listening
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of the story.

quiz.question: How does the central character approach their challenge?
options: Through thoughtful reflection, patience, and presence of mind
By shouting loudly and blaming friends
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in timeless fables.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach readers?
options: Patience, honesty, and humility lead to lasting harmony
quiz.hint: Think about how justice and truth prevail.
